Summary (full text)

Camera wyze-t20x-jxf23 (T20) in the light box with the SpyderCheckr 24 chart, lamps 3000 K. Both stacks ran on the same camera, the same chart position and the same light: the open stack (open-tx-isp + OpenIMP + timps) and the vendor stack (Ingenic ISP module + vendor libimp + timps built for it), one after the other.

Result: 58 pass, 0 fail, 109 info/warn, 1 flaky (failed 1 of 3, repeated), 1 planned checks not run in these runs.

Passed: frame luma p1_day (AE target, default comp 128); frame luma p1_night (AE target, default comp 128); chart grey RG (AWB, unclipped grey patches, 1.0 = neutral); chart grey BG (AWB, unclipped grey patches, 1.0 = neutral); p1_day dE00 mean, unclipped patches; p1_day dE00 mean, grey-normalised; grey row tone slope; MTF50 median of 8 chart edges (cycles/pixel); 10-90 % edge rise median (px); H.264 FixQP 25: decodes clean; ...

How to read: "pass" means the open stack is equal to or better than the vendor stack within the tolerance named in each row; matched-exposure rows (A2) compare the same integration time and gain on both stacks, read back from the ISP.

A5 Encoder (H.264): open vs vendor, same settings

Cells = open / vendor. Static chart scene, lamps on, day pinned, streamer restarted per case with a /tmp conf. Bytes per frame and P/I from ffprobe -show_frames (frames before the first IDR and, for CBR, the first seconds are ignored). PSNR / SSIM (luma) of every decoded frame (SSIM every 2th) against the mean image of the stack's own H.264 FixQP reference recording, so the ISP difference between the stacks drops out; sensor noise stays in (see the noise-floor row): an encoder that smooths noise can score higher than the reference. blk = blockiness of the error image (step across 8-px borders / step inside, 1.00 = no block structure); GOP drift = PSNR of the IDR minus the last P of the GOP. n/a = the streamer of that stack did not take the setting.

run-t20-1110-fulllogsvendorflagNo kernel oops, warnings, timeouts or driver resets appear in the log. RTSP streams (about 900 frames in 60 s each, 0 errors), snapshots, streamer restarts, hflip, OSD and config persistence all passed. The only flags are the BAD-uv-static NV12 layout in night mode (constant chroma of 128, likely expected for IR monochrome), mild overexposure noted by the vision checks, slower lamps-on AE/Iridix settling, and a dark colour picture in d1d4 that is probably due to test sequencing. The camera returned after the sysrq reboot with tx_isp_t20 and sensor_jxf23_t20 loaded.
anomalies: NV12 snapshots in night IR mode report layout BAD-uv-static with uv_static 7/7 on all three captures. U/V are exactly 128.00 in every frame. This is expected for monochrome IR night mode, but the layout check flags it as BAD., The d1d4 vision check reports the picture nearly black with no IR night mode active (still colour, noisy) after the switch back to pin_day. The lamps were apparently still off, so this may be test sequencing rather than a driver fault., Lamps-on AE settle took 4.20 s versus 0.87 s for lamps off. Iridix was still changing 8.11 s after onset (25 changes), which suggests slow or oscillating AE/Iridix convergence. This is informational only., Repeated vision notes of slightly overexposed or partially clipped top row and light grey patches near white in the stab, reload and nightir phases., The SSH connection was reset during the sysrq reboot restore. This is expected from a forced reboot, but the shutdown was not clean.; severity: low
run-t20-1110-fullcomparebothinfoBoth images have similar sharpness and noise, with no clear difference at this resolution. The vendor stack exposes and boosts brightness more aggressively: the top-row whites and the light-yellow patch blow out to near-white, and the reds and pinks get lighter and less accurate. The open-source stack keeps highlights intact, has a cleaner tonal ramp and gives more faithful colour, with only a mild warm cast. Overall the open-source image is better; the vendor image only wins on 'pop' and slightly lifted shadows.
better_overall: Picture 1 (open-source stack); open_better: Highlight handling: top-row bright neutrals and the light-yellow patch keep their separation instead of clipping to white, Tone/contrast: more controlled exposure with a more even gray-step ramp across the neutral row, Colour accuracy on bright patches: the yellow (row 2) keeps its hue, and pink and orange-red are less washed out, White balance: neutrals look fairly neutral and only slightly warm; vendor_better: Slightly brighter, punchier look overall, with more vivid yellow, yellow-green and cyan, Midtones and shadows are a touch lifted, so the dark patches and background look less murky, Saturation on the mid-tone blues and greens is marginally stronger
run-t20-1110-fulltriagebothinfoOnly one open-stack fail warrants follow-up: D4 day/night not returning to Day with lamps on (unclear, verify lux/thresholds). The RC bitrate step fail is a method artifact (restart-based, value on target, flaky). All vendor fails are references and look like harness issues (WB preset settle criterion, restart-related missing frames).
open bitrate step 2000 -> 4000 measured: invalid (Measured 3964 is within ~1% of target; failure stems from restart-based method (no live rc tool) and decode errors at restart, flaky 1/3, so a method problem rather than RC defect.) | open D4 lamps on: ISP day after 180 s: unclear (Staying in Night with lamps on for 180 s may be a real day/night switch defect, but could also be lamp level/placement or hysteresis thresholds; verify lux at sensor and compare vendor result.) | vendor time to a stable picture: WB preset 1 at 3000 K: invalid (Vendor reference; a fixed WB preset mismatched to 3000 K light likely never meets the stability criterion, so the settle metric is unsuitable for presets.) | vendor time to a stable picture: WB preset 3 at 3000 K: invalid (Vendor reference; same as preset 1, the stability detection likely does not fit fixed-preset WB under mismatched light.) | vendor h264 ref_qp10: invalid (Vendor reference; no decodable frames after restart points to capture/restart timing or unsupported setting in the harness, not our defect.) | vendor h264 ref_end: invalid (Vendor reference; same no-decodable-frames-after-restart pattern suggests harness/restart issue.)
run-t20-1110-5000logsopenflagNo kernel oops, warning, timeout or unexpected reset appears in the excerpt; the module reload at restore is a scripted step and looks clean. The camera itself responds normally: AE handles the lamps off/on switch in 2.5-3 s, and Iridix and exposure tracking look fine. Possible ISP firmware or driver issues are in white balance: auto WB failed to converge within 60 s, and presets 1, 4 and 8 return implausible grey ratios (e.g. 0.009/0.000). That points to bad preset gain tables or corrupt stats. Kernel dmesg was not included, so driver-level errors cannot be ruled out.
anomalies: 15:22:47 AWB auto at 5000 K did not stabilise within 60 s (>63 s, [fail]); R/G and B/G kept drifting (B/G 0.913 -> 0.895). This could be an ISP firmware AWB convergence problem or a test/scene issue., 15:23:22 WB preset 1 reports grey R/G B/G = 0.009 / 0.000, which is physically implausible. This suggests a broken preset, a near-black or corrupt frame, or wrong gains from the driver., 15:25:04 WB preset 4 reports R/G B/G = 0.032 / 2.421, an extreme and implausible result. Preset gains may be mis-programmed., 15:27:24 WB preset 8 reports R/G B/G = 0.309 / 1.882, a strongly skewed result that may also be a mis-programmed preset., WB presets 5 and 6 give nearly identical results (0.743/1.347 vs 0.743/1.350). The presets may be mapped to the same gains., Settle times vary widely between presets (22-42 s; presets 4 and 8 take 42 s). Slow or irregular application of controls is possible., 15:32:52 the restore step reloads the kernel modules (rmmod/modprobe tx_isp_t20 with isp_clk=100000000 and sensor_jxf23_t20). Method

  • Same camera, same chart position, same lamps; open stack first, then the vendor ISP module + vendor libimp are loaded from /tmp (nothing flashed); the camera returns to the flashed image at the end (module reload or reboot).
  • P1 = camera defaults (AE, AWB, comp 128). P2 = matched exposure: the same integration time and gains on both stacks, set inside the streamer and read back from the ISP; rows whose read-back differs are marked verify=FAIL and not compared.
  • A/A: point p2_a is measured twice (p2_a, p2_a2); the relative difference is the repeatability of the method. A difference between the stacks counts only beyond 2 x that spread (floor 5 %).
  • NV12 noise is measured on raw NV12 frames from the streamer (no JPEG in the path): temporal standard deviation per pixel over the burst, mean over Y 32..224, and U/V.
  • Colour: SpyderCheckr 24 detected automatically, sRGB -> Lab (D50), CIEDE2000 against the Datacolor default values (D50 assumed, not batch specific); 'grey-normalised' removes the white-balance cast first.
  • Sharpness: slanted-edge method on the chart's outer patch edges, frames averaged against noise; JPEG snapshot path.
  • SSIM/PSNR (when run): both stacks record the same static chart scene at the same bitrate; each stream is decoded and compared against a high-bitrate capture of the SAME stack (reference), so the number is the encoder loss of that stack; a cross-stack comparison on static frames is listed separately and includes the ISP difference.
  • Encoder (A5): both stacks get the same timps settings (codec, rc_mode, qp / bitrate, gop) through a /tmp conf and a streamer restart; the recordings come over RTSP (ffmpeg -c copy). The reference is a mean image, because single NV12 frames are not frame-aligned with the stream; the scene is static, so every decoded frame can be compared with it. A second reference at the end of the phase shows whether the scene or the AE moved in between.
  • Lamp switches are made by a person on a marker (NEED_* file); the times above are the marker times.
